newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hardie sees improved current year.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hardie sees improved current year.

text.p: Building products group James Hardie Industries Ltd said on Thursday it expected its profit after tax for the current year to March 31 to improve significantly compared to the past year.

James Hardie earlier reported a jump in net profit to A$83 million for the year to March 31, 1997, up from A$32.2 million in 1995/96. James Hardie managing director Keith Barton said in a statement the turnaround of underperforming Australian businesses remained a priority for the group, while continuing strong growth was expected in the United States.
Long-term prospects for all businesses remained attractive. Barton said the much heralded revocery in housing construction in Australia had yet to emerge to any significant degree.
"The modest recovery in Australian housing construction will not be sufficient to offset the impact of growing competition on our Australian fibre cement business," Barton said.
"Therefore, we expect volumes and earnings from this busienss to decline in the current year," he said.

Longer term, Hardid was modernising facilities and automating product finishing lines and accelerating new product development. "Several projects have been implemented to reduce working capital, overheads and functional duplication. In broad terms, the benefits of these projects will not be significant until the following year," Barton said.
Barton said the fundamental transformation of James Hardie in the past year was not fully apparent in the 1996/97 results.
The turnaround of the Australian fibre cement business, where earnings fell significantly in the past year, and the windows and pipelines businesses, which made losses, remained a priority, he said.
"These results were due mainly to the further 12 percent fall in housing construction, in calendar 1996, which had a severe impact on sales volumes and profit margins," Barton said.
He said a wide range of projects had been implemented to cut costs, respond to competition and expand markets for its products.

Barton said the company expected relatively stable market conditions in New Zealand but a modest decline in sales and profits compared to the strong performances of recent years, as competition intensified in major market segments.

"The building systems business should benefit from continuing strong demand for portable accommodation from the mining and resources sector and a steady performance is expected this year," Barton said.
"This business has significant longer term growth potential in Australia and Asia," he said.
In the United States, new construction was forecast to remain at or near current high levels and economic and interest rate conditions were expected to remain favourable.
"Volume and price are the key drivers of profitabilty from both the fibre cement and gypsum businesses," Barton said.
"Competiton in the U.S. fibre cement industry is growing as new entrants commission plants and existing participants expand capacity," he said.
